answer: ripple admits a ferrous only when three branch attestations come from branches with no shared ancestry; it fuses those branches atomically and checks the whole fused set at commit, so clones cannot reuse or split a triangle. Each admission burns tide equal to the live fused-branch count, attached to its ripple entry: the tenth costs ten, the thousandth a thousand, and a thousand clones burn 500,500 tide plus 3,000 fresh branches. It breaks if branches can be cloned or their ancestry rewritten.
